title: Cascade Ortho Rider Schedule — Takeover Cases and Changes of Orthodontist
content:
A takeover case under the Orthodontic Benefit Riders is treatment begun before the rider (or under another carrier). Whether such treatment is covered for its remaining months depends on the rider, as set out below.

| Rider | Takeover treatment covered | Least planned months of active treatment that must remain on the rider effective date | How a takeover case benefit is computed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cascade Ortho Rider Child 1000 | no | 0 | none |
| Cascade Ortho Rider Child 1500 | yes | 6 | remaining months prorated |
| Cascade Ortho Rider Child 2000 | yes | 6 | remaining months prorated |
| Cascade Ortho Rider Family 1500 | yes | 6 | remaining months prorated |
| Cascade Ortho Rider Family 2000 | yes | 3 | remaining months prorated |
| Cascade Ortho Rider Family 3000 | yes | 3 | remaining months prorated |

- **Minimum remaining months:** a takeover case is accepted only if at least this many planned months of active treatment remain on the rider effective date. The figure is 0 where takeover is not allowed.
- **Remaining months prorated:** the case benefit is multiplied by the months remaining and divided by the planned treatment months, and is paid as installments only.

## Changes of orthodontist (all six riders)

| Term | All six riders |
|---|---|
| Remaining benefit follows the patient to a new orthodontist | yes |
| Additional benefit for a new orthodontist's transfer or records fee | none: such a fee gets no benefit beyond the remaining case benefit |

*Hypothetical reading:* on a rider with a 6-month minimum, a takeover with 7 planned months remaining on the rider effective date meets the minimum and one with 5 does not. On a rider with a 3-month minimum, both would meet it.
